errors.description: Attempt 2 repeats the attempt-1 failure verbatim: both collar leaves still taper to sharp acute triangular tips despite maximum-emphasis wording that the leaf ends are cut off flat. The squared-off termination that defines this option is still completely absent.

errors.correction: Prompt-level emphasis has now failed twice; the model is anchored on the point-collar prior and on the blueprint photo's foreshortened near leaf, which it is reading as a point. notes: Attempt 2 of 2. Genuine improvements over attempt 1: the crop now cuts at the jawline with no mouth or lips in frame, the collar dominates roughly 60-65% of the frame, the two leaves mirror each other cleanly, a faint edge topstitch is now present, the background remains a clean seamless neutral light-grey with no props or architecture, and there is still zero text, annotation, watermark or dimension callout anywhere in frame. The tie is correctly absent and the top band button correctly unfastened. However the one thing that actually distinguishes this option — the flat squared-off collar point — failed identically to attempt 1: both leaves come to a sharp acute triangular tip. Escalated, explicit, repeated wording ('cut off flat', '~90 degree corner', 'two square corners', 'NOT a point collar', 'automatic rejection') did not move the model off its point-collar prior. Hard cap of 2 credit-spending generations reached; stopping. Do not publish candidate-2 — it would ship a visibly wrong collar to a paying customer. Recommended next step outside this run: re-reference with a tight crop of the squared leaf end, or a line-art profile of the truncated leaf, rather than the full-collar photo whose foreshortened near leaf is being misread as a point.
